transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-15 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Morris (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (NexaHealth CTO), Rajiv Singh (Head of ML Ops), Laura Perez (Security)
---
Summary (auto): Quick run-through of onboarding status, access setup, and initial pilot results. Focus on next steps for performance benchmarking and security signoff.
Topics: onboarding progress; VPC access / peering; SSO/SAML and KMS; preliminary benchmark results; tuning (batching, quant, cache); next steps for dedicated trial
---
[00:00] Samir: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. Uh, quick roll call — Samir here from Redwood, Elena is on the call, and then over to you, Maya, Rajiv, Laura — can you confirm?
[00:06] Maya: Yep hi, Maya here. Good to see you all.
[00:08] Rajiv: Rajiv — morning.
[00:09] Laura: Laura joining.
[00:11] Samir: Great. Agenda — 1) where we are with onboarding and access, 2) review the small test results you ran last week, 3) tuning recs from Elena, and 4) next steps. Sound good?
[00:20] Maya: Sounds good.
[00:22] Elena: Yep. I'll jump in on the perf bits.
[00:24]
[02:10] Rajiv: Quick update from our side on onboarding — we got the service account created, and we spun up a small test in our dev VPC. We saw roughly 220ms median latency for 256-token requests with the default model and about 3.2x cost vs our simple LLM baseline. These are very rough numbers, still tuning.
[02:35] Elena: Okay that's helpful. When you say 220ms that's end-to-end or just token generation?
[02:39] Rajiv: End-to-end, including our app front end. Generation alone looked closer to 140-160ms in the logs.
[02:45] Elena: Got it — so there's some network and app overhead. On the Redwood side the main levers are batching config, KV caching, and quantization profile. For low latency we usually recommend small batch sizes with prefix caching for conversational flows. For cost we can push a 4-bit quant profile that reduces GPU memory and can drop cost by ~30% in our trials, but there's a small quality delta to monitor.
[03:10] Maya: Right. For NexaHealth the quality delta can't be more than a few percent — our clinical summaries need high fidelity.
[03:17] Elena: Understood. We'll run quantization with your eval set and give you the quality vs latency matrix.
[03:22]
[05:05] Laura: From security — we need to confirm key management. We use AWS KMS and we want Redwood to support customer-managed keys and audit logging. Also SSO is a must.
[05:15] Samir: Absolutely. We support bringing your own KMS for Private deployments and Dedicated as well — for hosted we have envelope encryption but we can discuss a Private deployment for full CMK control. SSO — SAML/Okta is supported; we can supply metadata and do an integration call.
[05:36] Laura: Okay, SAML would be preferred. Also need SOC 2 and recent pen-test summary.
[05:42] Samir: We'll send our SOC 2 report and the third-party pen test summary after this call — I'll add that to the action items.
[06:00]
[08:00] Rajiv: A couple of things on networking — we attempted a VPC peering test but hit an IP routing issue; looks like our firewall rules blocked the port. We'll share the route tables. For the pilot we were hoping to use a peering connection to a Redwood dedicated endpoint, is that still the preferred path?
[08:20] Elena: Yes, for Private or Dedicated the usual flow is VPC peering or customer-hosted transit. We can also do a secure tunnel for the short term if peering takes longer. For the benchmark we prefer peering to minimize added latency.
[08:33] Rajiv: Cool. We'll open the ports and send details.
[08:36]
[10:12] Samir: On the test results — thanks for sharing the spreadsheet earlier. We pulled a couple of rows: mostly seq length 256 and 512. Your 256 runs show the 220ms median; 512 was closer to 460ms. The patterns look consistent with our expectations.
[10:28] Elena: For the 512s we suggest changing the compilation profile and enabling larger KV cache blocks — that reduces re-compute on long sequences. Also, if this is conversational we can enable prefix KV caching so repeated context doesn't get re-encoded every time.
[10:45] Rajiv: We do have long-ish histories in the workflow so caching sounds promising.
[10:48] Elena: Great — we'll prepare a config diff.
[11:00]
[13:00] Maya: A question on model variants — would Redwood fall back to a cheaper model if dedicated capacity is exhausted? We don't want failed requests.
[13:10] Samir: Yes, we have smart routing and automatic fallbacks — you can set a policy to accept a slightly cheaper variant during high load or route to hosted capacity as a backup. We'll show the routing policy UI in the next demo if helpful.
[13:28] Maya: Yes please, that would help with our SRE folks.
[13:32] Samir: Noted.
[13:35]
[15:20] Elena: On perf bench scheduling — we recommend running a dedicated-node benchmark for 1-2 hours with production-ish traffic (burst + steady). I can run that if you provide VPC peering and a test dataset, and then we'll return a token-level cost breakdown.
[15:37] Rajiv: We can assemble a dataset — maybe 500 requests that match our prod mix. We'll get that to you by Friday.
[15:45] Elena: Perfect. Also, small note: if you want to test quantized profiles we'll run both fp16 and 4-bit q runs so you can see tradeoffs.
[15:55] Rajiv: Good.
[17:05] Laura: One more thing on compliance — data residency. Some PHI-adjacent data needs to remain in us-east-1. Is that possible with Redwood Private?
[17:15] Samir: Yes, Dedicated/Private allow region pinning. For hosted we have region options but for strict residency you'd likely choose Private in your VPC or Dedicated in us-east-1. We'll document the options.
[17:27] Laura: Thanks.
[17:30]
[20:00] Maya: On timelines — our execs want a decision on moving to dedicated capacity by end of month. Do you have a short trial / pricing estimate we can use?
[20:15] Samir: We can provision a 2-week dedicated trial with limited nodes; I'll put together a preliminary cost sheet after we see the benchmark numbers. Expect a draft by Monday.
[20:26] Maya: That helps.
[20:30]
[22:40] Elena: I want to call out a tuning trick we used with another healthcare customer — switching compilation kernels for the attention path reduced p95 by ~12% for longer sequences. It's model and seq-length dependent but we'll try that in the run. Also consider raising concurrency caps on the client side to allow more continuous batching, but that may increase tail latency; we can tune for median vs p95 depending on your SLO.
[23:05] Rajiv: We currently cap concurrency to avoid large mem spikes; we'll revisit that after seeing the bench.
[23:12] Elena: OK.
[25:00] Samir: Quick product note — Redwood Optimize will suggest batching and quant profiles automatically once we onboard your traffic patterns. That can speed up ops post-pilot.
[25:15] Maya: Good to know.
[25:20]
[28:00] Laura: For the security pack, does the pack include encryption-at-rest details, key rotation cadence, and access logs?
[28:08] Samir: Yes — SOC2 and our security pack include KMS integration docs, key rotation policies, access logging and audit log samples. We'll include contact for a technical security call if you want deeper dive.
[28:22] Laura: Please do.
[28:25]
[32:00] Rajiv: Small transcription note from our test: some requests intermittently hit higher latency — around 1.2s — looks like cold start or maybe preemption on spot-like nodes?
[32:14] Elena: If you saw preemption it's likely because the test used shared hosted nodes. On Dedicated nodes you won't see preemption; if you plan to save costs with burst pools we can discuss fallback policies to avoid tail spikes.
[32:30] Rajiv: Good distinction — we'll aim for dedicated for the bench.
[32:35]
[36:00] Samir: Recap / action items: We'll send security pack (SOC2 + pen test), pricing draft for dedicated trial, and a Redwood contact for SAML setup. Elena will schedule and run the perf bench once VPC peering details and dataset are provided. Customer will share peering info, test data, and confirm KMS policy constraints.
[36:25] Maya: Sounds right.
[36:30]
[40:00] Laura: One final question — any limitations on token length for quantized runs?
[40:06] Elena: Quantization itself doesn't change max context window; but some quant kernels have different perf characteristics at very long contexts. We'll include that in the bench and the matrix.
[40:18] Rajiv: OK.
[40:22]
[45:00] Samir: Alright everyone, thank you. We'll send the items and set up the benchmark scheduling invite. I put tentative perf window for 2026-12-20 in the shared calendar — Elena will follow up with exact time.
[45:18] Elena: Yep I'll follow up with a run plan and the commands to run on your side.
[45:25] Maya: Appreciate it.
[45:27] Rajiv: Thanks all.
[45:30] Laura: Thanks.
[45:35] Samir: Meeting adjourned.
---
Notes: Some transcription labels/terms may be imperfect (KV cache -> KV cash, SSO slash SAML spoken as "SSO/SAML"). References to shared artifacts: security pack link (sent post-call), benchmark spreadsheet (already shared), and peering instructions doc (to be shared).
